en.name: Heilongjiang Province Museum

en.name: Harbin Jewish History and Cultural Exhibition

en.text: The cable car crosses the Songhua River, connecting the city center with the attractions on Sun Island.

en.text: This prominent riverside monument commemorates the citizens' successful fight against the 1957 flood.

en.name: Songhua River Railway Bridge
en.text: The former steel railway bridge now serves as a popular pedestrian walkway with panoramic views over the Songhua River.

en.name: Chocolate Museum
en.text: The museum is dedicated to the history of chocolate making and features elaborate sculptures made of cocoa.

en.name: Russian Oil Painting and Sculpture Collection
en.text: This gallery presents a collection of classical and contemporary Russian oil paintings and sculptures.

en.name: Beifang Theater
en.text: A cultural venue known for its performances of traditional Chinese opera and modern plays.

en.name: Harbin Juvenile Palace Art Center
en.text: This large arts center is dedicated to the promotion and training of young talents in music and visual arts.

en.name: Harbin Old Synagogue Concert Hall
en.text: The former synagogue now serves as a concert hall, renowned for its excellent acoustics during classical music performances.

en.name: Tatar Mosque
en.text: This distinctive Byzantine-style mosque was built in the early 20th century for the city's Tatar community.

en.name: Modern Hotel

en.name: Saint Sophia Cathedral
en.text: Completed in 1932, this former Orthodox church impresses with its massive green dome in Byzantine style.

en.name: Church of The Intercession
en.text: This active Russian Orthodox church is recognizable by its traditional onion domes and splendid icons inside.

en.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral
en.text: Harbin's Catholic Sacred Heart Cathedral stands out with its Gothic architectural elements and prominent red facade.

en.name: Podzemnyi produktovyi rynok
en.text: This underground food market offers a wide variety of local snacks, spices, and fresh ingredients.

descriptionAdvanced.de:
Touristen strömen vor allem zum weltberühmten Internationalen Eis- und Schneeskulpturenfestival nach Harbin, wo kolossale, beleuchtete Eisstrukturen ein magisches Winterwunderland schaffen. Jenseits des Eises bietet die Stadt eine reizvolle Mischung aus chinesischer und russischer Kultur, die in der historischen Central Street (Zhongyang-Fußgängerzone) und der ikonischen, zwiebelförmigen Sophienkathedrale sichtbar wird.

Harbins Küche spiegelt seine geografische Kreuzung wider und bietet herzhafte nordostchinesische Gerichte wie süß-saures Schweinefleisch (Guobaorou), Brot nach russischer Art, geräucherte Würstchen und das berühmte Madieer-Eis, das sogar bei Minusgraden gegessen wird.

Es ist durch den internationalen Flughafen Harbin Taiping und die umfangreiche Hochgeschwindigkeitsstrecke leicht erreichbar. Die beste Zeit für einen Besuch ist von Ende Dezember bis Februar, um das Eisfestival zu erleben, obwohl der Sommer auch angenehm kühles Wetter bietet, um der südlichen Hitze zu entfliehen.
descriptionAdvanced.hu:
A turisták elsősorban a világhírű Nemzetközi Jég- és Hószobrászati Fesztivál miatt özönlenek Harbinba, ahol a kolosszális, kivilágított jégépítmények varázslatos téli csodaországot teremtenek. A jégen túl a város a kínai és orosz kultúrák bájos keverékét kínálja, amely a történelmi Központi utcán (Zhongyang sétálóutca) és az ikonikus, hagymakupolás Szent Szófia-székesegyházon is megmutatkozik.

Harbin konyhája tükrözi földrajzi helyzetét, kiadós északkelet-kínai ételeket, például édes-savanyú sertéshúst (Guobaorou), orosz stílusú kenyereket és füstölt kolbászt kínálva. A híres Madieer fagylaltot még a leghidegebb téli fagyban is előszeretettel fogyasztják a helyiek és a turisták.

A Harbin Taiping repülőtéren és a kiterjedt nagysebességű vasúton keresztül könnyen megközelíthető. A látogatás legfőbb ideje december végétől februárig tart a jégfesztivál miatt, bár a nyár is kellemesen hűvös időjárást kínál a déli hőség elől menekülőknek.
descriptionAdvanced.ro:
Turiștii se adună la Harbin în primul rând pentru Festivalul Internațional de Sculptură în Gheață și Zăpadă, de renume mondial, unde structurile colosale, iluminate, de gheață creează o țară a minunilor magică de iarnă. Dincolo de gheață, orașul oferă un amestec fermecător de culturi chinezești și rusești, vizibil pe strada istorică centrală (strada pietonală Zhongyang) și emblematica catedrală Sfânta Sofia, cu dom în formă de ceapă.

Bucătăria din Harbin reflectă răscrucea sa geografică, oferind mâncăruri consistente din nord-estul Chinei, cum ar fi porcul dulce-acru (Guobaorou), pâine în stil rusesc, cârnați afumați și faimoasa înghețată Madieer, consumată chiar și la temperaturi de îngheț.

Deservit de Aeroportul Internațional Harbin Taiping și de o cale ferată extinsă de mare viteză, este ușor accesibil. Momentul suprem pentru a vizita este de la sfârșitul lunii decembrie până în februarie pentru a experimenta festivalul de gheață, deși vara oferă, de asemenea, vreme plăcut răcoroasă.
descriptionAdvanced.en:
Tourists flock to Harbin primarily for the world-renowned International Ice and Snow Sculpture Festival, where colossal, illuminated ice structures create a magical winter wonderland. Beyond the ice, the city offers a charming blend of Chinese and Russian cultures, visible in the historic Central Street (Zhongyang Pedestrian Street) and the iconic, onion-domed St. Sophia Cathedral.

Harbin's cuisine reflects its geographical crossroads, offering hearty Northeastern Chinese dishes like sweet and sour pork (Guobaorou), Russian-style breads, smoked sausages, and the famous Madieer ice cream, famously eaten even in freezing winter temperatures.

Served by Harbin Taiping International Airport and extensive high-speed rail networks, it's easily accessible. The ultimate time to visit is from late December to February to experience the massive ice festival, though summer also offers pleasantly cool weather for escaping the southern heat.
